question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
**Six months** from the date the offer of employment in the Institute is made.

- Officers/employees may "opt out of employment in the Institute" by doing so "within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [621/2025 §33(2)(b)].
- Those who decline are paid compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme, with Ministerial and Finance Ministry approval [621/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: Source is the GS version (2025-07-17); the same text also appears in 629/2025, and committee-stage changes are not covered.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
Under the Inland Revenue (Amendment) bill, the exclusion applies to amounts deducted under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act “for any year of assessment prior to April 1, 2018” [013/2026 §37].

- Subsection (2) does not apply even if an “un-deducted balance” of that deduction remains as at April 1, 2018 [013/2026 §37].
- This is the new section 202(2A)(a) of the principal enactment [013/2026 §37].

Caveats: The evidence names the bill “Inland Revenue (Amendment) - GS” (GS, 2026-02-24), with identical text in 022/2026; only the Gazette version is shown, not any presented Bill.

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
A moneylending licence issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24 is “valid for a period of one year” and must specify its expiry date [645/2025 §25(c),(d)].

- A licence to carry on the **microfinance business** itself is instead “issued for a period of three years” [645/2025 §32(7)].
- Section 32(9) applies only specified parts of section 25, omitting paragraph (c), which supports the three-year microfinance licence [645/2025 §32(9)].

Caveat: evidence is the GS dated 2025-11-17 (identical in 653/2025); no committee-stage text is included.

warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 078/2026 §1

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
A renewal application must be submitted "not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued" [657/2025 §6(1)].

- It must also be in the prescribed Form with the prescribed renewal fee [657/2025 §6(1)].
- The same clause appears in the presented Bill [007/2026], so the GS (2025-12-12) and Bill (2026-01-20) texts match on this point.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer: The overall maximum is now **three years**, replacing “a period of two years” [033/

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
The levy is calculated monthly — charged "on the value of the supply of telecommunication services ... in respect of each month," in the substituted section 2 [028/2026 §2].

- Applies to "every person receiving any telecommunication service," at rates set in the new Schedule [028/2026 §2].
- Diplomatic Privileges Act No. 9 of 1996 persons/organisations are exempt [028/2026 §2].
- The text is identical in Bill 035/2026 (presented 2026-05-06) to the GS version 028/2026 (2026-04-23) [028/2026 §2], [035/2026].

Caveats: No specific rate or penalty is given in the quoted clause; rates sit in the Schedule, which is not reproduced in the evidence.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
The amended section 49(5) allows notice of dishonour to be given **in writing, by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means** that sufficiently identify the bill and intimate that it was dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment [601/2025 §8].

- The electronic/fax notice must “sufficiently identify the bill” and state the dishonour ground [601/2025 §8].
- The same §8 text appears in 612/2025, a Bill dated 2025-06-17 [601/2025 §8].

Caveat: the quoted text is from the GS version 601/2025; the evidence says 612/2025 carries identical text.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
Under the Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation (Incorporation) Bill [626/2025 §11(4)], "qualified auditor" means either an individual member of a recognised institute holding a practising certificate, or a firm whose resident partners each hold one.

- Individual: a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka "or any other Institute established by law" who "possesses a certified to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute" [626/2025 §11(4)(a)].
- Firm: "a firm of Accountants each of the resident partners" of which is such a member holding that practising certificate [626/2025 §11(4)(b)].
- The audit itself is done by a qualified auditor "appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [626/2025 §11(3)].

Caveats: The text appears identically in 607/2025 and the quoted wording ("a certified to practice") is as printed; "certified" appears to be a typographical variant of "certificate". No year was specified in your question — this is the 2025-07-23 Bill.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
It is defined in the interpretation clause as "activities designed to facilitate to exchange of ideas, skills, and experiences fostering on culture of learning and collaboration" [646/2025 §18].

- Source is the GS version of the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation) bill, published 2025-11-20, with identical text in 002/2026 [646/2025 §18].
- The quoted wording reproduces the text verbatim, including its drafting slips ("facilitate to exchange", "fostering on culture") [646/2025 §18].

Caveats: Only this definition clause is in evidence; no provision describing actual activities is available.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
Under the newest Bill (**047/2026, 2026-06-25**; the GS **041/2026, 2026-06-11** is identical on this clause), the Society may “take and hold any property, movable or immovable” and may “sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of” it [047/2026 §13].

- Such property must be held for the purposes of the Act and subject to the Society’s rules under section 7 [047/2026 §13]; those rules cover “administration and management of the property” [047/2026 §7].
- It may purchase, rent, construct, renovate or otherwise obtain lands/buildings and deal with or dispose of them as the Council determines [047/2026 §6].
- It may also administer a lawful trust or “any real or personal property” to promote its objects [047/2026 §6].

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
The President of the Institute chairs both: the proviso to §18(2) states that "the President of the Institute shall be the Chairman of the Committees referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b)" — i.e. the Membership Committee and the Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee [637/2025 §18(2)].

- Other committees: each must include "at least, one member of the Council and such member shall be the Chairman of the Committee" [637/2025 §18(2)].
- If more than one Council member sits on a committee, "the Council shall appoint one of such members as the Chairperson" [637/2025 §18(3)].
- Composition, powers and functions of each committee are to be set by rules under the Act [637/2025 §18(4)].

Caveats: This is the GS version (Gazette 2025-10-01, also in 656/2025); the text names the office of President, not an individual, and does not give a separate selection method for chairs beyond §18(2)–(3).

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under the substituted section 35, employees of businesses licensed **before** the section commences get a three-year income-tax exemption, while employees of businesses licensed **on or after** that date are taxable.

- Pre-commencement licensees: "any employment income of a resident employee ... shall be exempt from income tax" and deemed a permissible credit to a personal foreign currency account; non-resident employees are likewise "exempt from income tax" and not liable on foreign-earned income [652/2025 §3(2)(a)-(b)].
- Post-commencement licensees: "Any employment income of a resident employee and a non-resident employee ... shall be liable to income tax" [652/2025 §3(3)].
- Salaries of pre-commencement licensees must be paid "in a designated foreign currency, other than in Sri Lanka Rupees" [652/2025 §3(1)].

Caveats: Text is identical in the GS (652/2025, 28 Nov 2025) and the presented Bill (654/2025, 5 Dec 2025). The clause fixing when the three years begins is garbled in the evidence ("commencing from the Short title ... month immediately following"), so the start date is unclear.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The long title is amended by substituting the words "freight forwArders And non-VesseL operAting common cArriers" for "freight forwArders, non-VesseL operAting common cArriers, And contAiner operAtors" — i.e. "container operators" is dropped from the long title [658/2025 §2].

- The same clause appears identically in the presented Bill [005/2026], per the note on [658/2025 §2]; the GS is dated 2025-12-12 and the Bill 2026-01-20.
- Consequential renaming strips "and Container Operators" from the Act's short title in the principal enactment and other written law [005/2026 §3].
- §4 also deletes the definition of "container operators" in section 15 [005/2026 §4].

Caveats: I rely on the text quoted at [658/2025 §2], which the evidence states is identical to the Bill version; the Bill's §2 text itself is not reproduced.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The evidence does not contain a general statement of the amendment's overall purpose; it shows only specific sectional changes. The matching bill is **029/2026** (Bill, 2026-04-09), whose GS counterpart is **018/2026** (2026-03-11).

- The Schedule substitutes wording across many sections — e.g. "funds or property" replaced by "funds, property or other assets, material support or resources" in sections 3(1), 4(1), 4B, 4E, 4F [018/2026 §2; 029/2026 p.20].
- §16 repeals the "funds or property" definition and substitutes "funds, property or other assets", and inserts new definitions including "armed conflict", "computer system" and "foreign terrorist fighter" [018/2026 §16].
- §4 amends section 3: repeals the proviso, adds aiding/abetting, organizing, accomplice and contribution offences, and inserts subsection (2B) on collecting funds for terrorist training, travel or foreign terrorist fighters [018/2026 §4].

Caveats: no passage summarises the amendment's overall effect; penalty figures and time limits appear only in auto-generated summaries, not in the quoted clause text.

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
The **Appropriation Bill 639/2025** (presented 2025-09-26) is the 2025 bill providing for government spending and borrowing for the financial year 2026; an earlier version, **632/2025** (2025-09-17), carries identical §2 text.

- Authorises estimated expenditure of "rupees four thousand four hundred thirty-four billion three hundred fifty-six million four hundred sixty-eight thousand" for 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026, met from the Consolidated Fund or other government funds [639/2025 §2(1)].
- Authorises borrowing in FY2026, in or outside Sri Lanka, capped so the outstanding balance "shall not exceed rupees three thousand eight hundred billion", with loan details in the Final Budget Position Report under s.51 of the Public Financial Management Act, No. 44 of 2024 [639/2025 §2(1)].
- Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund is stated as rupees four thousand five hundred forty-five billion six hundred forty-three million five hundred thirty-two thousand for the same period [639/2025 §2(4)].

Caveats: The bill-level summaries are auto-generated hints; figures above are quoted from §2. Committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
It is the **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation)** bill — presented version [055/2026] (Bill, 27 July 2026), preceded by the Gazette version [043/2026] (GS, 15 June 2026); note 055/2026's short title spells it "Recourses".

- Objects include "developing, promoting, establishing, expanding or modernising all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" and empowering "rural, estate and underserved communities" [043/2026 §3].
- It incorporates existing members as a body corporate with perpetual succession, deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [043/2026 §2].

Caveats: The two versions' text is stated to be identical; the auto-generated summaries are hints only — no penalties are set out.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
The maximum is **one year**: the Council may, "in lieu of disenrolling a member," "warn, reprimand or suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year" [054/2026 §24]. This is from the bill titled "Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media" (Bill, 2026-07-22), which matches the name in your question.

- The power arises only where the Disciplinary Committee's report under s.23(3) establishes professional misconduct [054/2026 §23; 054/2026 §24].
- The Council may later re-enroll the person at its discretion if satisfied they are fit to be a member and act as a media professional [054/2026 §24].

Caveats: the same text appears in 040/2026 and 050/2026; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
More than three months: the person must be in "lawful occupation" and have had "undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation" of the premises for "a period of more than three months" before the events in sections 3, 4 or 5 [004/2026 §2].

- The identical test appears in the earlier Gazette version [634/2025 §2].
- Note the statutory wording is "undisturbed and uninterrupted", not "peacefully"; lawful occupation is a separate requirement [004/2026 §2].

Caveats: I relied on the Protection of Occupants Bill 004/2026 (Bill, 2026-01-20), which matches the title; the GS version 634/2025 (2025-09-18) uses the same wording, so no difference appears.

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
**Seventy years.** Section 9(i) of the Gambling Regulatory Authority Bill disqualifies a person from appointment to the Board if such person "is over seventy years of age".

- Same text appears in both versions: Bill [613/2025 §9(i)] (presented 2025-06-17) and GS [594/2025 §9(i)] (gazetted 2025-05-27), so no difference between them on this point.
- The bar is framed as a disqualification for appointment, and it sits alongside other disqualifications in the same section [613/2025 §9].

Caveats: This is the disqualification list as reproduced; committee-stage amendments are not in the corpus, and the section does not expressly say whether a member is also barred from continuing past 70.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
The maximum jail term is **one year**: “imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year” [021/2026 §31].

- This applies to arriving in or leaving Sri Lanka with cash or bearer-negotiable instruments above the Minister-specified sum without reporting [021/2026 §31].
- The same clause also allows a fine “not exceeding three times of the value” of the cash/instruments, or both [021/2026 §31].

Caveat: this is the Gazette version dated 2026-03-17, not the presented Bill; committee-stage amendments are not in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
Under the Sri Lanka Cricket bill, a member who misses the deadline owes a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription" [072/2026 §30(4)].

- Deadline for the annual subscription is 31 December of the preceding year; the doubled fee is payable by 30 April of the following year [072/2026 §30(3)–(4)].
- Failing to pay both by that later date means the member "shall automatically forfeit its voting right" [072/2026 §30(5)].
- Six months after that due date, non-payment leads to removal from the Register of Members [072/2026 §30(6)].

Caveats: The evidence is the Gazette version ("Sri Lanka Cricket - GS", 2026-09-28, p.32), with identical text noted in 077/2026; the amount is expressed as a multiple of the subscription, not a fixed figure.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The bill does not set a payment deadline. It only fixes which debts are caught: those "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" must be paid by the body corporate [009/2026 §12].

- No day is prescribed for actual settlement — the text states the obligation, not a time limit [009/2026 §12].
- The same wording appears in the 2021 bill, Indira Cancer Trust (Incorporation), GS 2021-08-23 [095/2021 §12].

Caveats: I rely on the Indira Cancer Charitable Trust (Incorporation) GS of 2026-02-05 (identical text in 014/2026); no presented "Bill" version or committee amendments are in the evidence.

warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 014/2026 §1

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Under the Immigration Bill, the offence carries a fine of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than five hundred thousand rupees" [082/2026 §90(2)].

- The duty is to notify an Immigration Officer when a transit passenger or crew member fails to continue their journey in circumstances suggesting they remained in Sri Lanka [082/2026 §90(1)].
- Liability falls on the master, captain or agent, and is "jointly and severally" on conviction [082/2026 §90(2)].
- The text specifies a fine only — no term of imprisonment is mentioned [082/2026 §90(2)].

Caveats: I rely on the bill titled "Immigration" [082/2026], dated 2026-10-07; the same text appears in 508/2024, 513/2024 and 071/2026. Note the separate, heavier fine in §89(3) (500,000–1,000,000 rupees) applies to failure to comply with removal/receiving directions, not this reporting duty.

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
The evidence does not state how long the Board Chairman serves. No passage in the extract addresses the Chairman's term of office, so the question cannot be answered from it.

- [631/2025 §15] amends section 18 of the principal enactment: in subsection (4), "four" is replaced by "three"; the extract does not say what that subsection governs, so it cannot be tied to the Chairman's tenure.
- [631/2025 §15] also changes subsection (5) to require "the approval of the majority of the members of the Board," and replaces subsection (6) with a rule-making provision on meetings and business.
- [631/2025 §18] concerns the Director-General's qualifications and functions, not the Chairman.

Caveats: The bill is the Gazette version (GS, 2025-09-04); the term-of-office provision, presumably elsewhere in the principal enactment or Bill, is absent from the evidence.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
The evidence shows the term is substituted, not defined: references to "Controller"/"Rubber Controller" become "Director-General" [595/2025 §2], and in other laws, notices, contracts or forms they are read as "Director-General of the Rubber Development Department" [595/2025 §2(2)]. The same text appears in the presented Bill [620/2025 §2].

- The amendment substitutes the words "Director-General" for "Controller" and "Rubber Controller" "wherever such words appear in the principal enactment" [595/2025 §2(1)].
- It applies "from and after the date of commencement of this Act" to other written laws and documents [595/2025 §2(2)].
- Newest version: Bill 620/2025 (presented 2025-07-09), earlier GS 595/2025 (2025-05-28).

Caveats: The auto-generated summary says a new definition of "Director-General" is added and the old "Controller" definition deleted, but that definition clause's text is not in the evidence, so the precise statutory definition cannot be confirmed.

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
Under the amendment in the Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Bill, 2025-05-08, "public authority" means "a Ministry, any Department or Provincial Council, local authority, or a Ministry or Department of Provincial Council", but excludes "a public corporation" and "a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007" [591/2025 §13(2)].

- The change is made by repealing and substituting the definition of "public authority" in section 56 of the principal enactment [591/2025 §13(2)].
- Same text appears in 575/2025; the 2021/2022 bills (152/2021, 167/2022) do not contain this substituted definition [167/2022 §47].

Caveats: Based on the text supplied, which is garbled in places (e.g. "Ministry or Department of Provincial Council"). If the enacted version widens the list to statutory bodies or government-held companies, that wording is not in the evidence given.

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
A crop qualifies if it is identified as having "export potential in addition to the local consumption", is not one of the excluded food crops, and is declared by the Minister as "a notified agricultural crop" under section 2 [045/2026 §5].

- Excluded: "paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops", and any crop identified as a plantation crop [045/2026 §5].
- The definition replaces the one in section 19 of the principal enactment (Act No. 46 of 1992) [045/2026 §5].

Caveats: This is the definition in the GS version (2026-06-25); the Bill version is 060/2026 (2026-08-07), whose clause text is not reproduced here beyond being described as identical [045/2026 §5].

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
Under the Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka (Incorporation) bill [597/2025 §10(4)], "qualified auditor" means either:

- an **individual** who is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka "or any other institute established by law" and "possesses a certificate to practice as an Accountant, issued by the Council of such institute" [597/2025 §10(4)(a)]; or
- a **firm of accountants** whose resident partners each meet that same membership-and-certificate requirement [597/2025 §10(4)(b)].

The audit itself is conducted by such an auditor "appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [597/2025 §10(3)].

Caveats: This is the Gazette (GS) version, 2025-05-29; the same text appears in 608/2025. No presented-Bill text is in the evidence, so any differences cannot be checked.

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer: In the Proceeds of Crime Bill (1 Mar 2025; §60 text identical in the GS of 21 Feb 2025), an investigation officer may use: controlled delivery; digital surveillance, including “interception and recording of digital, voice, video communication”; undercover operations including decoys; “laying of traps”; and forensic extraction from computers, mobile phones, storage devices and other digital equipment [570/202

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five members, and yes — the quorum must include the Chairperson: "ﬁ ve members including the Chairperson" [054/2026 §7(2)].

- The same rule appears in the Gazette version: "ﬁ ve members including the Chairperson" [040/2026 §7(2)], which notes the text is identical in 050/2026.
- Quorum may be met in person or by audio-visual means where all can see and hear each other [054/2026 §7(3)].

Caveats: The bill title in the evidence is "Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media" (Bill, 2026-07-22); the GS is dated 2026-06-05. Committee-stage amendments are not covered.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
Section 19 inserts a new section 38A: the Commission computes fares by a formula it determines, "adhering to the national policy relating to transportation fares approved by Parliament", and specifies them "by Order published in the Gazette" [592/2025 §19]. Each provider must then prepare its fare list from the Commission's website list and display it "at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle" [592/2025 §19].

- The Commission publishes fares "in the official website of the Commission" and may inspect compliance under section 39(2); failure is "guilty of an offence under section 40" [592/2025 §19].
- The formula is set after "considering the written representations of the relevant stakeholders", with periodic revision [592/2025 §5].

Caveats: The text does not state the penalty for the section 40 offence, nor the Gazette/approval procedural steps; those provisions are not in the evidence.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
The Mass Foundation is a body corporate with "perpetual succession" under the name "Mass Foundation", may "sue and be sued", and is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [025/2026 §2]. The same clause text appears in both versions: GS 025/2026 (2026-04-08) and Bill 037/2026 (2026-05-07).

- Seal: not to be affixed to any instrument except in the presence of two Committee members who sign it, independently of any witness; kept in the custody of a Committee office bearer it decides [025/2026 §15].
- Classification: the Act No. 31 of 1980 provisions apply "to and in relation to the management of the affairs" of the body corporate [025/2026 §2(2)].

Caveats: neither version's text on these points differs; committee-stage amendments are not in the corpus.

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
Under the new section 57a, for an industrial estate or industrial park the phrase is read as the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka (under BOI Law No. 4 of 1978) under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution, or the Minister assigned the subject of industries, “as the case may be” [053/2026 §10].

- The two alternatives are stated in the alternative, not cumulatively; the text does not say which applies where [053/2026 §10].
- For a community based organization the reference is instead “the Minister assigned the subject of community based water supply” [053/2026 §10].

Caveats: The same text appears in 019/2026 §10 (Bill, 2026-03-13) and 053/2026 §10 (Bill, 2026-07-21) — the latter is the newer version; I found no gazette (GS) version in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under [078/2026 §33], the magistrate must visit the "approved place of detention" in his jurisdiction "once a month" "without giving any advance notice" to the authority in charge, and inspect it.

- At each visit he must interview suspects and "look into their well-being", and call for and inspect "detention registers, Detention Orders and other books and documents" [078/2026 §33(1)].
- If he observes or is told of torture or "cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment", he "shall forthwith make an order" for production before a Judicial Medical Officer, with the report submitted to him [078/2026 §33(4)].
- If satisfied on reasonable grounds, after hearing the suspect and the police officer, he "shall act in terms of section 31" [078/2026 §33(5)].

Caveats: Text is from the Bill version dated 2026-10-06 (identical in 070/2026); the magistrate before whom the suspect was first produced has separate visiting powers under §33(2).

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill (Bill 622/2025, 11 July 2025; text identical in GS 616/2025, 3 July 2025), mediation covers "civil and commercial disputes" generally, but not disputes assigned to the older mediation statutes or those needing a court decree.

- Covered: disputes mediated under a mediation agreement, "voluntarily referred to mediation by a party" without one, or "referred by a court of law" [622/2025 §2(1)].
- Excluded: disputes mediable under the Mediation Boards Act, No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act, No. 21 of 2003 — which also cannot be submitted under this Act [622/2025 §2(2)–(3)].
- Also excluded: disputes whose settlement "requires the inclusion of terms that can be given effect to only on a decree or order of court", including the schedule items — dissolution/nullity of marriage, minors and persons of unsound mind, adoption, probate, insolvency, admiralty rights in rem, fundamental-rights breaches — though related matters "may be mediated" to submit terms to court [622/2025 §3; 616/2025 §30 schedule].

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
The accounts of Samurdhi community-based banking societies must be audited under Article 154 of the Constitution (public corporation audit provisions) and the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018 — inserted as new section 35A of the Samurdhi Act, No. 1 of 2013 [600/2025 §3] (identical in 614/2025).

- The Bill also covers community-based *banks* separately, under new section 28A, with the same two audit frameworks [600/2025 §2].
- No new penalties are introduced; the duty is a statutory audit obligation [600/2025 §3].

Caveats: The newest text is Bill 614/2025 (17 June 2025); the GS version 600/2025 (4 June 2025) carries identical wording, so no differences appear. Committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
The newest text — Companies (Amendment) GS [582/2025 §17] (2025-04-24) — lets a struck-off company apply to court, within ten years, to be re-registered and recover its property; the identical rule appears in [541/2024 §15] (2024-08-06).

- Remedy: apply to court with the Attorney-General a party, "before the expiry of a period of ten years", showing cause why it could not comply; the court may "permit the re-registration of the company" and order return of "all property previously vested in the State" [582/2025 §17].
- Limits: third-party rights acquired from the State "in good faith shall not be affected", and the State is not liable where property was destroyed or damaged or possession was never taken [582/2025 §17].

Caveats: these are Gazette (GS) versions of two separate bills; the 2025 text differs only in referencing "the Companies (Amendment) Act, No. .. of 2025" rather than "this amendment Act".

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
Under Bill 063/2026 §17 (Anti-Corruption (Amendment), Bill, 19 Aug 2026), bail is refused where the amounts cross stated thresholds and the Director-General certifies them; release is then possible only "in exceptional circumstances by a High Court."

- Bribe of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees" solicited, accepted or offered [063/2026 §17].
- Loss to the Government, or a benefit/favour/advantage to himself or another, of "not less than five hundred thousand rupees", "the value of which has been confirmed by the Director-General by issuing a certificate" [063/2026 §17].
- Otherwise all offences are "cognizable and non-bailable as per the provisions of the Bail Act, No. 30 of 1997" [063/2026 §17].

Caveats: only this clause is in evidence — the proviso text is garbled ("soliciting, accepting or offering of section 149 of the principal enactment a bribe"), and no other bail provisions are supplied.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
Offences in Part B of the Schedule to the Extradition Law are deemed **not** to be offences "of a political character or an offence connected with a political offence or an offence inspired by political motives" when extradition is between Sri Lanka and any UN Member State [073/2026 §11] (Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters – GS, 30 Sep 2026; identical text in 085/2026).

- The deeming applies "for the purposes only of extradition" of a person accused or convicted of such an offence, and to "affording assistance to a UN Member State under section 12" [073/2026 §11].
- It operates "Notwithstanding anything in the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977" [073/2026 §11].

Caveats: §8 inserts the new offence item "immediately before Part B" of that Schedule, not expressly within Part B; no Bill-stage text is in the evidence.

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the substituted Section 23r(2) of the National Environmental bill, conviction by the Magistrate having jurisdiction carries a fine of "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees", plus "a fine of five thousand rupees for each day" the offence continues after conviction [032/2026 §18].

- This replaces the earlier range of "rupees ten thousand" to "rupees one hundred thousand", with the daily fine raised from "rupees five hundred" to five thousand [032/2026 §18].
- Source is the Bill version dated 2026-05-06 (identical text also in 026/2026) [032/2026 §18].

Caveats: No Gazette ("GS") version is in the evidence, and the quoted text is the amending clause, not the consolidated section.

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The amendment replaces Section 42's fine with "a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or ... imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year or to both" [611/2025 §13].

- The offence previously carried "a fine not less than five thousand rupees and not more than twenty five thousand rupees", which the amendment removes [611/2025 §13].
- Evidence is from the Gazette version only; the same text appears in 619/2025 [611/2025 §13].

Caveats: The passage does not state what conduct Section 42 of the principal enactment penalises, and no presented "Bill" version is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
A penalty of "two thousand rupees" plus the registration fee payable under section 5, and the local authority must itself "take steps to vaccinate and register such dog immediately" in the Register of Dogs.

- Time allowed first: "fourteen days" by notice, extendable by a further fourteen days for reasonable cause [076/2026 §7(2)–(3)].
- Penalty: Rs. 2,000 "in addition to the registration fee payable under section 5 to the local authority" [076/2026 §7(4)].
- Additional action: registration in the "Register of Dogs referred to in section 8" [076/2026 §7(4)]; that register is kept by each local authority [066/2026 §8].

Caveats: Text is identical in GS 066/2026 (2026-09-07) and Bill 076/2026 (2026-09-24); the latter is the presented version.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The amendment adds "methamphetamine" to the named-drug list in section 54A(1)(a) and creates a new offence of manufacturing other Group A–E dangerous drugs [068/2026 §2].

- List change: substitutes "heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine" for "heroin or cocaine or morphine or opium" [068/2026 §2].
- New offence: manufacturing any dangerous drug in Groups A, B, C, D and E in Part I of the Third Schedule, "other than heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium and methamphetamine" [068/2026 §2].
- Penalty: on conviction by the High Court "without a jury", a fine "not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees", or imprisonment "not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years", or both [068/2026 §2].

The Gazette version [062/2026 §2] (2026-08-24) has the same clause text as Bill 068/2026 (2026-09-08). Caveats: the auto-generated summary's points on bail and the Third Schedule/cannabis rest on sections 3–5, not the clause quoted above.

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No. Once the repeal commences, those benefits cease: former presidents and widows will "no longer be provided with or paid to" them.

- The cut-off covers any residence or monthly allowance, monthly secretarial allowance, official transport and "such other facilities", and the widow's monthly pension — all in respect of the period "preceding the date of commencement" [624/2025 §3(a)-(c)].
- The mechanism is simply repeal of the Presidents' Entitlements Act, No. 4 of 1986 [624/2025 §2]; the auto-summary likewise says no new powers, duties or penalties are introduced [627/2025].

Caveats: Both versions — GS 2025-07-31 and Bill 627/2025 of 2025-08-07 — carry identical clause text. Committee-stage amendments are not in the evidence.

warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 627/2025 §1

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
The amendment inserts section 316a, punishing “voluntarily caus[ing] grievous hurt to a person under eighteen years of age” with imprisonment “which may extend to ten years”, plus a fine and possible court-ordered compensation [618/2025 §6]. The same text appears in Bill 630/2025 (Bill, 2025-08-19) [630/2025].

- The court may order compensation after considering a victim-impact statement from the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses [618/2025 §6].
- The offence is subject to the exception “provided for by section 326” [618/2025 §6].

Caveats: The evidence says “grievous hurt” and “voluntarily”, not “serious injury” or “intentionally”; it does not give a separate fine amount for section 316a.

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
Section 5(1) is amended so the "sixty million rupees" four-quarter threshold applies only "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026", and a new paragraph (d) sets the limit for later periods at **thirty-six million rupees** [017/2026 §3] (identical text also in 023/2026).

- In paragraph (b), "hundred and twenty million rupees; or" becomes "hundred and twenty million rupees;" — the disjunctive "or" is dropped [017/2026 §3(1)].
- In paragraph (c), "sixty million rupees." becomes "sixty million rupees; or" [017/2026 §3(2)].
- New (d): "for any period commencing on or after April 1, 2026, the aggregate turnover of such registered person for a period of consecutive four quarters does not exceed thirty-six million rupees" [017/2026 §3(3)].

Caveats: the quoted §3 text is garbled and does not restate the full existing wording of paragraphs (b) and (c), so the complete before/after turnover figures cannot be fully reconstructed from the evidence. Newest version is Bill 023/2026 (2026-03-17); 017/2026 is the GS (2026-03-03).

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment raises the ownership threshold in Section 14(1) from "more than fifty per centum" to "one hundred per centum", and replaces "person" references in subsections (2) and (3) with a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007 — [584/2025 §12].

- Subsection (1): "more than fifty per centum" substituted by "one hundred per centum" [584/2025 §12].
- Subsection (2): "Any person who" becomes "Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which" [584/2025 §12].
- Subsection (3): "a person who" becomes "a company, which" [584/2025 §12].

Caveats: This is the "Sri Lanka Electricity (Amendment) - GS" (2025-05-16, identical text in 599/2025); the evidence does not show the surrounding subsections' full wording.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
Paragraph (n) of Section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance (Chapter 87) is repealed, and in paragraph (p) the definition of "express trust" is narrowed by replacing "trust generally in the form" with "trust in the form" [081/2026 §2].

- The amendment is made by the Trusts (Amendment) Bill (GS, 2026-10-14), which also appears as 086/2026 with identical text [081/2026 §2].
- Section 3 was last amended by Act No. 6 of 2018 [081/2026 §2].

Caveats: The evidence does not reproduce the full text of paragraphs (n) or (p), so the practical effect of the repeal and the exact wording of the resulting definition cannot be stated.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
Under the Judicature (Amendment), the retirement age for certain judges rises from "sixty-one years" to "sixty-three years", while "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years" [058/2026 §3].

- The 62-year rule applies "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355)" [058/2026 §3(2)].
- These are substitutions into s.6(3) and a repeal-and-replacement of s.6(4) of the Judicature Act, No. 2 of 1978 [058/2026 §3].

Caveats: The same s.6 text appears in the Gazette bill 058/2026 (2026-08-07) and the presented Bill 064/2026 (2026-08-18); no differences are shown, and committee-stage amendments are not included.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
A person may serve as Dean of a Faculty for **no more than two terms** [649/2025 §2].

- The clause states: “No person shall be appointed as the Dean of a Faculty for more than two terms” [649/2025 §2].
- This text appears in Bill 655/2025 (2025-12-03) and GS 649/2025 (2025-11-21), which are identical on this clause [649/2025 §2].

Caveats: Committee-stage amendments are not included.

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation)** Bill 2025 — Bill **628/2025** (presented 2025-08-06), whose earlier Gazette version is **623/2025** GS (2025-07-18), with identical text.

- Clause 2(1) creates the "body corporate" named the "Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka", with "perpetual succession", power to "sue and be sued" and a common seal [623/2025 §cl.2(1)].
- It succeeds to the existing Institute's debts and liabilities, which "shall be paid or discharged by the body corporate hereby constituted" [623/2025 §3].
- Its objects include upholding "the professional standards of the Facilities Management profession" [623/2025 §2(2)].

Caveats: no clause number is shown for sub-clause (2); text is from the GS version, stated to be identical in 628/2025.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 623/2025 §2
citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 628/2025 §12, 628/2025 §15, 628/2025 §17

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
The Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Bill — Bill 596/2025, presented 8 May 2025 (Gazette version 581/2025, 10 April 2025).

- It makes the Foundation's members "a body corporate with perpetual succession", able to sue and be sued and to use a common seal [596/2025 §2].
- The first Board must be appointed or elected "within one year of the date of commencement"; office bearers hold three-year terms [596/2025 §5].
- Rules need a two-thirds vote of members present and go before Parliament within three months of gazetting [596/2025 §7].

Caveats: Both versions appear; the above cites the Bill. The summary is auto-generated and mentions no penalties.

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
The 2026 amendment is the **Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment)** bill, published as GS 008/2026 on 2026-02-05 (identical text also in Bill 016/2026, presented 2026-02-19) [008/2026 §2] [016/2026].

- It amends Section 32 of the principal enactment, substituting paragraph (a) with "Adultery by the husband or wife after marrige." [008/2026 §2] [016/2026].
- It also repeals paragraph (b) of Section 32 [008/2026 §2].
- Short title: "Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment) Act, No. of 2026" [008/2026 §1].

Caveats: The quoted text spells "marrige"; the auto-generated summary renders it "marriage" — the clause text controls.

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
It is the **Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation)** bill — Bill **039/2026** as presented to Parliament on 2026‑05‑21, an earlier version having been published as Gazette bill **024/2026** on 2026‑04‑08; both carry the same operative clause.

- §2(1): members "shall have perpetual succession under the name and style of the 'Al‑Hashimi Association'" and may "sue and be sued" with a common seal [024/2026 §2].
- §2(2): the body corporate is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [024/2026 §2].

Caveats: the evidence gives no clause-level text for §3–§19 of 039/2026 beyond headings; committee-stage amendments are not included.

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 059/2026, the Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Bill (presented 2026-08-04), whose §2 states: "The Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 is hereby repealed" [059/2026 §2].

- It also abolishes the offices: the Chief of Defence Staff and Committee members "shall cease to hold such office" from commencement [059/2026 §3(1)].
- The same repeal text appears in the earlier Gazette version, Bill 036/2026 (GS, 2026-05-15) [036/2026 §2].

Caveats: The evidence marks the clause text of 059/2026 and 036/2026 as identical; the summaries are auto-generated hints only.

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Bill, No. 605/2025 (presented 5 June 2025; earlier Gazette version 589/2025, 22 May 2025), amends the Provincial Councils Elections Act, No. 2 of 1988 [605/2025 §1].

- §2 restores the 1988 provisions "in force on September 21, 2017" notwithstanding Act No. 17 of 2017, operative from the Act's coming into force [589/2025 §2].
- Acts done from 22 September 2017 onward are preserved "insofar as such act is not inconsistent with" the 1988 Act [589/2025 §2].
- §3 provides the Sinhala text prevails over Tamil on inconsistency [589/2025 §1 outline; 605/2025].

Caveats: Only the short title, §2 and the §3 outline appear; full clause text is not in the evidence.

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment)** bill amends the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016 — Bill **602/2025** (presented, 2025-06-03), with an earlier Gazette version **587/2025** (GS, 2025-05-20) [602/2025 §2; 587/2025].

- It substitutes date ranges in section 3: "For the period commencing on May 1, 2015 and ending on March 31, 2025" and "for the period commencing on January 1, 2016 and ending on March 31, 2025" [602/2025 §2].
- Operative date: provisions "deemed to have come into operation on April 1, 2025" [602/2025 §1(2)].

Caveats: The auto-generated summaries call it an "extension"; the clause text only fixes the end date at March 31, 2025. Whether the 2016 Act is best described as a "financial assistance scheme" is your paraphrase, not the text's wording.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) Bill** — Bill **604/2025**, presented 3 June 2025 (Gazetted version **586/2025**, 20 May 2025) — amends section 3 of the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016 [604/2025 §2] [586/2025].

- It sets the minimum monthly wage at "twenty-seven thousand rupees" from 1 April 2025 to 31 December 2025, rising to "thirty thousand rupees" from 1 January 2026 [604/2025 §2].
- Budgetary relief allowances under the 2005 and 2016 Acts are to "form part of" that minimum wage [604/2025 §3].
- It is "deemed to have come into operation on April 1, 2025" [604/2025 §1].

Caveats: Earlier bills (537/2024, 040/2021) amend the same 2016 Act; the 604/2025 and 586/2025 texts shown are identical.

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
The **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment)** bill, which amends the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 36 of 2005 — presented as Bill 603/2025 (2025-06-03), earlier published as GS 588/2025 (2025-05-20).

- It substitutes in section 3(1) the words "With effect from August 1, 2005" with "For the period commencing on August 1, 2005 and ending on March 31, 2025" [588/2025 §2].
- Both versions carry identical clause text [588/2025 §2; 603/2025].
- Sinhala text prevails over Tamil in any inconsistency [588/2025 §3].

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
Bill 001/2026, the **Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) - Bill** (published 2026-01-07), is the 2026 legislation: clause 2 states "The Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977 is hereby repealed." [001/2026 §2]

- Its long title/short-title provision is the "Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal)" Act [001/2026 §4].
- It was presented by the Minister of Justice and National Integration [001/2026].
- An auto-generated summary says it also stops pensions already being paid under that law and related 1982/1990 provisions — a hint only, not clause text; the repeal clause itself is §2 [001/2026 §2].

Caveats: Only the Bill version (not a Gazette version) is in evidence, and the text of §3 (the "for the avoidance of doubt" clause) is truncated.

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment) Bill — Bill 642/2025, presented on 21 October 2025 — amends the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988 [642/2025]. Its earlier Gazette version is Bill 640/2025, published 2 October 2025 [640/2025].

- Both set the levy at "fifteen per centum" for years from 1 April 2023 "but ending prior to October 1, 2025", and "eighteen per centum" from 1 October 2025 [640/2025 §2(1)].
- Both double the casino entrance levy from "United States Dollars fifty" to "United States Dollars one hundred" [640/2025 §2(2)].
- The 1988 Act was last amended by Act, No. 11 of 2023 [640/2025 §2].

Caveats: only the Gazette text of 640/2025 gives clause detail; I have no clause text for the presented Bill 642/2025, so I cannot confirm the two versions are identical.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
The best 2025 match is **Bill 625/2025, "Land Development (Amendment)"** (Bill, 22 July 2025), with an earlier Gazette version, **617/2025** (GS, 4 July 2025) carrying identical clause text.

- It repeals "or upon his or her marriage" from subsection 48A 2(c) and repeals subsection 48B 1(a) [625/2025 §2] [617/2025 §3].
- It substitutes "fails without reasonable cause to succeed" for "fails to succeed" in section 68(1) [625/2025 §4].

Caveats: The clause text never names the principal enactment as "Chapter 464"; that reference appears only in the accompanying long-title/description, so on the clause text alone the link is not proven. Two other 2025-adjacent versions are noted in the evidence: 617/2025 (GS) and 519/2024 (2024, not 2025).

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The **Finance (Amendment) Bill, No. 034/2026** (Bill, 2026-05-06) amends the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018 [034/2026 §2]. The same text appears in the earlier Gazette version, **027/2026** (GS, 2026-04-23) [034/2026 §2].

- It amends only section 44, substituting wording on the cellular tower levy [034/2026 §2].
- New towers commencing commercial operations "on or after January 1, 2026" are exempt "for a period of five years" [034/2026 §2].
- Subsection (2) is made "Subject to the provisions of subsection (1)" [034/2026 §2].

Caveats: Bill 034/2026 states §2 is "identical text also in 027/2026"; I have no text showing any difference between the GS and Bill versions.

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
The 2026 bill is the **Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Bill, Bill 056/2026** (presented 22 July 2026), amending Act No. 47 of 1956 [056/2026 §1][056/2026 §2]. An earlier Gazette version, **GS 044/2026** (25 June 2026), has the same title [044/2026].

- It replaces “ten thousand rupees” with “one hundred thousand rupees” in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20a(3) [056/2026 §2][056/2026 §3][056/2026 §4].
- The higher penalties do not apply to offences committed before the amendment operates [056/2026 §5].
- If the Sinhala and Tamil texts conflict, the Sinhala text prevails [056/2026 §6].

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
The **Online Safety (Repeal) Bill, No. 590/2025** (published as a Bill on 2025-05-08; GS predecessor **578/2025**, 2025-04-08) — its title matches the question, and it states: "The Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 is hereby repealed" [578/2025 §2; identical text also in 590/2025].

- Regulations made under the 2024 Act after its enactment are also repealed from the date this Act is enacted [590/2025 §3].
- Short title: "Online Safety (Repeal) Act, No. of 2025" [590/2025 §1].

Caveats: The bill-level summaries describing the 2024 Act's internet-platform and content-moderation scope are marked auto-generated hints only; the clause text evidences only the repeal.

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The 2025 bill is the **Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions)** bill — GS 565/2025 (published 2025-01-01) and the presented Bill 566/2025 (2025-01-09) — covering the local authorities listed in its Schedule whose 2023 polls were postponed.

- Prior nomination papers are "deemed to be of no force and effect as if such nomination papers had never been submitted" [565/2025 §2(1)], and the old nomination notices are revoked [565/2025 §2(2)].
- Fresh section 26 nomination notices are to be published on a date the Election Commission determines by Gazette Order, "not later than three months from the date of coming into operation of this Act" [565/2025 §3].
- Candidate deposits are refunded on production of the receipt issued under section 29(3) [565/2025 §2(3)].

Caveats: the text in evidence sets no fresh polling date itself — only the three-month deadline for nomination notices; the polls date is referred to in the preamble but not fixed in the clauses shown.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill — Bill 650/2025, presented 14 November 2025** (Gazette version 643/2025, 7 November 2025) amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008 [650/2025 §2].

- It substitutes “ten years” for “twenty-five years” as the maximum tax-holiday period [650/2025 §2].
- It requires a Ministry of Finance ex-ante cost-benefit analysis, with a recommendation “within one month” of referral [650/2025 §3].
- Non-compliant project entities get a show-cause period of “one month”, after which benefits may be restricted, suspended or revoked [650/2025 §4].

Caveats: the two versions differ only in presentation (presenting minister); no clause-level differences are shown in the evidence.

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
Bill 010/2026, the **UnV Foundation (Incorporation)** Bill (presented 22 January 2026), is the version before Parliament; its earlier Gazette version is 003/2026 (9 January 2026).

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
Bill 576/2025, the Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment) — GS, published 2025-03-28 — amends the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979 [576/2025 §2].

- It inserts new sections 144A and 144B on dispensing with a suspect's or accused's personal attendance in court [576/2025 §2].
- It also inserts sections 273A–273U on evidence given via "contemporaneous audio-visual linkage" [576/2025 §5], and adds Forms 24 and 25 to the Second Schedule [576/2025 §6].
- Identical text appears in bill 579/2025 [576/2025 §2, §5, §6].

Caveats: The evidence does not show whether 576/2025 and 579/2025 differ in any respect, nor their presentation status.

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
Bill **065/2026, "Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution"** (Bill version, 2026-08-18), presented by the Minister of Justice and National Integration; its Gazette predecessor is 057/2026 (GS, 2026-08-07).

- §2 repeals and replaces Article 107(5): retirement "shall be sixty-seven years" for Supreme Court Judges and "sixty-five years" for Court of Appeal Judges; the Chief Justice retires at 67 or after "six years" in office, "whichever occurs earlier" [065/2026 §2].
- §3 amends Article 137, substituting "not more than twenty four other Judges" for "not more than nineteen other Judges" [065/2026 §3].
- Short title: "This Act may be cited as the Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution" [057/2026 §1].

Caveats: The cited clauses are identical in 057/2026 and 065/2026; the auto-summary's "67 to 67 (no change)" wording is imprecise, so rely on the clause text. Separately, unrelated 2024 bills (493/2024, 460/2024) share the same title.

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 006/2026, the **Rent (Repeal) Bill** (Bill, 2026-01-20), states: "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed" [006/2026 §2].

- It is the only 2026 bill in the evidence; the earlier equivalents are 526/2024 and 555/2024 (GS, 2024-07-19) [526/2024 §3].
- The repeal is subject to one-year transitional protections, e.g. no ejectment suits and no rent above the "authorised rent" for "one year from the relevant date" [006/2026 §3(a)-(b)].
- Pending Rent Board/Board of Review matters must be concluded within that same one-year period [006/2026 §3(d)-(e)].

Caveats: The bill's title is "Rent (Repeal)", not "Tenancy Act"; the repealed statute is Act No. 7 of 1972 as cited in the text.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
The **Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children (Incorporation)** Bill — the presented version is **015/2026 (Bill, 2026-02-18)**, preceded by **011/2026 (GS, 2026-02-06)**; their clause texts are stated to be identical [011/2026 §2] [015/2026].

- It converts existing members of the Centre into members of a body corporate "with perpetual succession" that may "sue and be sued" and use a common seal [011/2026 §2(1)].
- The body corporate is deemed a Voluntary Social Services Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [011/2026 §2(2)].
- Its objects include IT-related training and skills programmes for rural youth, without discrimination [011/2026 §3].

Caveats: The enacted corporate name in §2 is "Mahawilachchiya Centre for Education for Children", which differs slightly from the Bill's title; and the evidence does not show whether the Bill has since been enacted.
